summary.headline: Q1 FY27 DI pipe volumes fell 27% YoY to 1.20 lakh tons; consolidated EBITDA Rs 139 crore at 9.5% margin, guided to 12-13% by Q3-Q4 FY27.
summary.overview:
Standalone and consolidated volumes fell sharply on weak domestic DI pipe demand, with export volumes also hit by Middle East tensions. Management reported consolidated EBITDA of Rs 139 crore (9.5% margin) and PAT of Rs 48.4 crore, while standalone PAT was only Rs 5.9 crore. Management pointed to JJM 2.0 sanctions and irrigation/river-linking pipelines for an H2 FY27 recovery, cut FY27 DI volume expectations to about 5.75 lakh tons, and announced diversification into industrial paints, valves and railway rubber components. Consolidated net debt was Rs 876 crore at 30 June 2026, down about Rs 1,100 crore in FY26.</overview>

segments.name: DI pipes and CI pipes (standalone core)
segments.commentary: Q1 volume 1.20 lakh tons, down 27% YoY; FY27 volume now guided at about 5.75 lakh tons versus earlier 6.5-7.0 lakh tons. Order book about 3 lakh tons (about five months), roughly 50% from JJM.

segments.name: T.I.S. Service S.p.A. (Italy, acquired)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about EUR 10 million with EBITDA margin about 13-14%. FY27 exit target EUR 42-45 million revenue, 14-15% EBITDA margin, about 8% PAT margin.

segments.name: Valves
segments.commentary: Valve revenue about Rs 400 crore; Q1 growth stated at 18% on last year's Q1. Target to double in four years; Indian valve facility to start by end of FY27. Exports from Italy plant to shift partly to India.

segments.name: Industrial paints and protective coatings (new)
segments.commentary: Initial investment about Rs 100 crore for 17,000 kilolitres capacity via brownfield expansion in West Bengal; long-term target Rs 800-1,000 crore revenue and Rs 250-300 crore capex over 4-5 years. Commercial production expected from Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Railway rubber components (gasket plant, Andhra Pradesh)
segments.commentary: Board approved entry today; railway registration expected in 4-6 months; some additional equipment under installation, expected in about three months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 DI pipe and CI pipe volume about 5.75 lakh tons (management said close to last year's level), with better revenue and margin per ton.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected at 12-13% in Q3 and Q4 FY27; Q2 FY27 expected to be at least similar to Q1 levels.
Export share expected at 22-25% of total volumes by end FY27.
Growth expected mainly in H2 FY27 as JJM 2.0 disbursements pick up; management said the Rs 70,000 crore JJM outlay may drive a significant uplift in Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28.
FY30-FY31 aspiration of consolidated revenue Rs 7,000-8,000 crore at 13-13.5% EBITDA margin.
Dependence on DI pipes to fall from about 85% to about 55% in four to five years.
capex_capacity: Industrial paints: about Rs 100 crore initial investment for 17,000 kilolitres in West Bengal; phased capex Rs 250-300 crore over four to five years.
Valve plant in India to commence operations by end of FY27, first phase in West Bengal; Asian subcontinent expected to contribute 40-45% of valve business in three to four years.
Ferro alloy: second plant planned adjacent to existing unit at brownfield site; capacity increase in ferroalloy business under consideration.
Management said about Rs 200 crore to be spent in West Bengal over the next year; greenfield Odisha site put on hold; about Rs 700 crore of capital available for investment including acquisitions.
Term debt about Rs 340 crore, scheduled to fall to about Rs 230 crore.
demand_pricing: Central JJM allocation Rs 67,670 crore for FY27; about Rs 10,344 crore sanctioned to states year to date versus Rs 1,560 crore released under JJM in the previous year. Management said about Rs 6,000 crore released so far.
Q1 FY27 production about 1.0-1.1 lakh tons versus about 1.8 lakh tons in Q1 FY26, per management.
Management expects about 12-13% of JJM outlay to come to Company (stated for DI industry share), and 5-7% of irrigation project volumes to convert into DI pipes.
Saudi Arabia accounts for about 2-3% of sales; management expects 1-1.5% to be lost, to be diverted to other GCC and African markets.
Export mix: about 60-70% Western markets (Europe, UK), remaining 40% Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia.
Management called current DI realisation levels rock bottom and the worst DI year in India since 1994.
States active under JJM 2.0: Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Tamil Nadu; UP and Rajasthan expected to pick up.
